Fifteen comments

Navvie on the line

Surprised that this is not here already - perhaps it is under a different name

↳ Posted by Alancorsini on April 4th, 2005.

This one’s attributed to James Hill

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on April 4th, 2005.

Navvy On the Shore

There’s a reel version with the above title already here. It’s the one most commonly associated with the Bothy Band Recording.

↳ Posted by Bill Reeder on April 5th, 2005.

Different tunes?

I don’t see what this has to do with the reel the Bothy Band recorded, apart from the name, and them both being in “G”.

↳ Posted by Kenny on April 5th, 2005.

London Hornpipe

I know this as “London Hornpipe”, again an American fife and drum crossover tune.

↳ Posted by FyfferGuy on April 5th, 2005.

Different Tunes?

I know this tune has nothing to do with the Bothy Band recording. It’s just that this hornpipe shows up as the tune listed on the Bothy Band page. If you were looking for the tune by the Bothy Band, you would be disappointed. No big deal - that’s just the way the software works.

↳ Posted by Bill Reeder on April 5th, 2005.

Canadian Reel

We play this in New England under the name of Reel de Montreal. Dr. Dow-- is it on one of Hill’s tune books?

↳ Posted by David Levine on February 21st, 2014.

This is definitely a James Hill composition from the 19th century. It cannot be claimed as a Canadian tune - sorry. I have commented on Reel de Montreal before here https://thesession.org/tunes/1346. It seems to have been cobbled together for square dancing as a 20th century composite of other tunes from the English/Scottish traditions.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on February 22nd, 2014.

The Navvie On The Line, X:2

Setting as played at the Golden Guinea pub session, Bristol, UK.

↳ Posted by Mix O'Lydian on May 29th, 2015.

Re: The Navvie On The Line

In Middleton’s Selection (Keith, 1870), edited by Peter Milne, this tune is given the title “Ewan’s Hornpipe”.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on June 26th, 2021.

Re: The Navvie On The Line

… and in the Athole Collection (1884) it’s called “Evans”.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on August 14th, 2021.

The Spring Time

This is the final tune in the set of three hornpipes on Con Durham’s CD: https://thesession.org/recordings/5880
I daresay someone will tell me it’s on here already under a different title but I can’t find anything like it. The tune titles on the CD are a bit suspect so may well be known by another name.

↳ Posted by Tonypib on September 17th, 2023.

Re: The Spring Time

Correct.
https://thesession.org/tunes/4376

↳ Posted by Kenny on September 17th, 2023.

The Navigator, Seinn Port

This is the version of the Navigator as it’s found in the Seinn Port 112 Great Session Tunes issued by Comhaltas.

↳ Posted by Peter Supper on December 18th, 2023.

The Navvie On The Line, X:7

If I remember correctly I learned this setting from a home cassette recording of a folk program on BBC Radio Scotland sometime in the early 90s. Unfortunately the cassette is long gone so I have no idea who originally played it like this.

↳ Posted by bagpie on January 19th, 2025.

The original link is thesession.org/tunes/4376
